judul: Asset Forfeiture Bill: expert and two bar associations ask for due process safeguards, with a 15 December target for passage
teks: Commission III of the DPR held a public hearing (RDPU) during the constituency break (reses) to hear input on the Criminal Asset Forfeiture Bill (RUU Perampasan Aset Tindak Pidana) from a legal expert, the national board (DPN) of the Indonesian Advocates Association (Peradi), and the Indonesian Advocates Association Nasional Bersatu (AAI). The first expert gave six points of appreciation and nine critical notes, including a proposal for value-based confiscation (value based confiscation) to recover the gap between the state losses found by auditors and the restitution (uang pengganti) set in court rulings. Peradi stressed five due process "safeguards": forfeiture without a criminal prosecution should only be a complement, the burden of proof must remain with the authorities, judges must grant permission and supervise, owners must have a right to object, and good-faith third parties must be protected. AAI Nasional Bersatu proposed an independent asset management body or, at the least, an independent oversight body, and considered several articles inconsistent. The meeting chair said 68 resource persons have been heard and the target for passage is 15 December. Asset Forfeiture Bill Due process Property rights Advocates The meeting was held during the constituency break (reses) with permission from the DPR leadership. The chair said that, in principle, all the resource persons asked that this bill not become a tool of power or an abuse of power by the authorities. The first expert presented 15 points: 6 points of appreciation and 9 critical notes on the draft bill, which is a DPR initiative. The expert welcomed the coverage of 13 predicate crimes, the limited use of non-conviction based (NCB) forfeiture that requires a predicate crime, and the requirement that every stage of freezing and seizure go through a judge's order. The expert proposed keeping the identity of whistleblowers confidential, because legal protection alone is not enough if whistleblowers face physical threats. Among the critical notes: the phrase "other economic crimes" (tindak pidana ekonomi lainnya) in Article 4 paragraph 2 should be spelled out or removed, and each offense needs its own parameters. The expert proposed value-based confiscation so that the gap between the state losses found by auditors and the restitution (uang pengganti) in the ruling can be pursued, and so that the non-retroactivity principle is applied to the predicate crime. The expert also proposed that only the Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) and the Finance and Development Supervisory Agency (BPKP) be authorized to calculate state losses, and that the time frame (tempus delicti) for proving unexplained wealth be limited to the period since a person took office. Peradi said that asset forfeiture rules already exist in the Anti-Corruption Law (UU Tipikor) and the Anti-Money Laundering Law (UU TPPU) but have not been used to their full potential, and noted that it had not received an official copy of the draft before the meeting. Peradi put forward five due process safeguards: subsidiarity, in rem forfeiture without a finding of guilt, tiered burden of proof, judicial permission and supervision with a right to object, and protection of good-faith third parties. Peradi asked for objective indicators for the status of "fleeing" (melarikan diri), such as a wanted-persons listing (DPO) or an Interpol red notice, and for a minimum standard of proof of "more likely than not". Peradi asked that asset forfeiture not be turned into a value target to be achieved, because pressure to meet targets could create moral hazard. AAI Nasional Bersatu proposed an independent asset recovery center, not under the Attorney General's Office (kejaksaan), and stressed international cooperation such as mutual legal assistance and extradition. AAI Nasional Bersatu cited an ongoing case in which, in their view, seized assets were damaged and lost with no clarity on who is responsible. The next AAI resource person considered several articles inconsistent, for example the definition of forfeiture in Article 1, which requires a final and binding court ruling, while Article 3 also provides for forfeiture without a criminal verdict. The chair said 68 resource persons have been heard, further input can be sent by letter, and the target for passage is 15 December.

judul: Asset Forfeiture Bill: experts, lawyers and students give input to Commission III
teks: Commission III of the DPR held a public hearing (Rapat Dengar Pendapat Umum, or RDPU) on the Asset Forfeiture Bill (RUU Perampasan Aset) during the parliamentary recess (reses), saying it wanted to speed up the bill's passage. According to the meeting chair, this was roughly the 58th to 60th RDPU for this bill. Three parties gave input. Yadi Suryadi Putra of the Open Parliament Institute said he does not agree with the bill: in his view, existing rules (the Criminal Code, the Anti-Corruption Law and the Anti-Money Laundering Law) already cover asset forfeiture and reversed burden of proof, and he considers the experience of many countries to be problematic. The JAMAK lawyers' network said it supports fighting corruption but rejects including illicit enrichment in the bill. The Nusantara Student Alliance (AMAN) supports passing the bill with caution and presented 10 recommendations. Commission III members asked about foreign interests, oversight of law enforcement officers, the falling value of seized assets, and the scope of the criminal offenses covered. The meeting chair said that illicit enrichment is not included in the bill. The meeting took in input and made no decisions. Asset Forfeiture Bill Illicit enrichment Criminal law Citizens' rights The meeting chair said the RDPU was held during the recess to speed up passage of the Asset Forfeiture Bill; around 80 elements of society are scheduled to be heard in total. Yadi Suryadi Putra (Open Parliament Institute) said he does not agree with the bill and presented a political-economy review as well as practices in other countries. He named three main issues behind bills of this kind: illicit enrichment, asset forfeiture without a criminal verdict (non-conviction based, or NCB), and reversed burden of proof. He said Indonesia already has rules on asset forfeiture and reversed burden of proof, including in the Anti-Corruption Law, the Anti-Money Laundering Law (TPPU) and Supreme Court Regulation (PERMA) 1/2013. JAMAK rejected illicit enrichment on three grounds: the right to property under the 1945 Constitution, the presumption of innocence and legal certainty, and the absence of any international obligation to adopt it. AMAN presented 10 recommendations, including making the criminal route the main mechanism, treating NCB as a limited exception, transparent asset management, and a review every 5 years. Member Hinca Panjaitan proposed that underwater assets, such as sunken ships that endanger shipping, also be discussed as objects of forfeiture. The meeting chair said that illicit enrichment is not included in the bill.

judul: Cabinet session on two years of government: economy, capital markets, food, energy, and forest fires
teks: The Plenary Cabinet Meeting (Sidang Kabinet Paripurna) on 21 October 2026 marked two years of President Prabowo Subianto's government. The broadcast portion consisted of reports from ministers and heads of agencies. The Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs reported economic growth of 5.45 percent, inflation of 3.28 percent, and a fourth-quarter stimulus package that includes food aid, wage subsidies, and discounted tickets for the Christmas and New Year holiday period (Nataru). The head of the Financial Services Authority (OJK) reported Rp1.5 trillion in sanctions over coordinated trading in the capital market, following a warning from MSCI. The Minister of Investment reported realized investment of Rp3,923.2 trillion over the two years. The Coordinating Minister for Downstreaming and the Minister of Agriculture reported on fuel (BBM) and rice stocks, while the head of the National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) and the National Police Chief reported on the handling of forest and land fires (karhutla) and the related law enforcement. The President closed with directions on single-gateway exports, enforcement action within the free nutritious meals program (MBG), and teamwork. Government Economy Capital market Food Forest fires The Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs reported economic growth of 5.45 percent, inflation of 3.28 percent, and unemployment of 4.65 percent, which the minister described as the lowest since 1994. Fourth-quarter stimulus: rice food aid of 10 kg per month for 33.24 million beneficiary families (KPM), a wage subsidy of Rp300,000 for 13.3 million workers, and a 30 percent discount on Nataru (Christmas and New Year) tickets. Plans starting in January: a national internship program for 150,000 participants, a national vocational program for 300,000 participants, and income tax (PPh) borne by the government for salaries of up to Rp10 million. The head of the OJK explained the MSCI warning about a possible downgrade of Indonesia's market status, and reported Rp1.5 trillion in sanctions over coordinated trading. The Minister of Investment reported realized investment of Rp3,923.2 trillion from October 2024 to September 2026, with 5.48 million jobs absorbed. Danantara (the state investment management agency) reported that 364 state-owned enterprises (BUMN) have been streamlined or closed, with a target of 700 by the end of December. Coordinating Minister Bahlil Lahadalia stated that the fuel (BBM) disruption in Bali was caused by delays in distribution ships, not by a shortage of national reserves. Minister of Agriculture Amran Sulaiman reported rice stocks in warehouses of 4.56 million tons and a plan to cultivate 500,000 hectares of mineral swampland together with the military (TNI) without clearing primary forest. The National Police Chief reported on forest fire law enforcement: 243 individual suspects and 13 corporate suspects, with 23 reports recommended for permit revocation. The President gave directions on single-gateway exports to curb smuggling and under-invoicing. The President said 353 people were dishonorably discharged in connection with the implementation of the MBG program and called for enforcement to continue until the problem is fully cleaned up.

judul: Commission X hears P2G, JPPI and Perisai on the fate of teachers in the Sisdiknas Bill
teks: Commission X of the DPR (House of Representatives) held a public hearing (RDPU) on teacher governance in the revision of the National Education System Law (Sisdiknas), which would merge the Sisdiknas Law, the Higher Education Law, and the Teachers and Lecturers Law. The meeting chair stressed that the draft in circulation is not yet an official document. P2G (a teachers' association) proposed five pillars of teacher governance (competence, welfare, recruitment, distribution, protection), an article on a minimum wage for teachers, and a National Teacher Management Agency. JPPI (an education watchdog network) asked that teacher needs be calculated from the number of students, that the government be required to guarantee a minimum base salary for teachers including non-civil-servant teachers, and that the division of authority between the central and regional governments be made clear. Perisai, a coalition of private-school teacher organizations, asked for equal treatment of private and public school teachers and access to the P3K selection (the government contract-employee recruitment). The meeting produced three conclusions, including a reaffirmation of the 20 percent education budget. Education Teachers Sisdiknas Bill Education budget The meeting chair said the Sisdiknas Law revision uses a codification approach (merging three laws into one), and that the draft in circulation is still internal drafting, not an official document. P2G said some part-time P3K teachers are paid Rp50,000 to Rp200,000 per month, and that teachers have not received their professional allowance (TPG) for about the last four months. P2G argued that teacher governance overlaps among regional governments, the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Kemendikdasmen), the Ministry of Religious Affairs (Kemenag), the Ministry of Social Affairs (Kemensos, which runs the Sekolah Rakyat, or People's Schools), and the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology (Kemendiktisaintek, which runs the Garuda Superior High Schools), and questioned the fate of Sekolah Rakyat teachers, all of whom are P3K. P2G proposed five pillars of teacher governance: competence, welfare, recruitment, distribution, and protection. P2G said public schools still need 464,000 civil-servant teachers, while civil-servant (PNS) teacher recruitment has practically stopped since 2019. P2G put forward 21 recommendations, including an article on a minimum wage for teachers, early childhood education (PAUD) teacher pay equal to the provincial minimum wage (UMP), a locked-in 20 percent education budget, an AI protocol in education, and a National Teacher Management Agency. JPPI said the existing laws do not discriminate against teachers, but the bill must make clear that teacher needs are calculated from the number of students, not the number of schools. JPPI said 95.4 percent of madrasah teachers are employed privately, and proposed wording that the government must guarantee a minimum base salary for teachers, including non-civil-servant teachers. JPPI doubted that centralizing teachers would automatically solve the problems, citing madrasah teachers who are already centralized under Kemenag, and asked for a clear division of authority between the central and regional governments. Yayasan Cahaya Guru (part of JPPI) said teachers carry a load of up to 40 teaching hours per week on top of other duties, and asked for balanced protection for both teachers and students. Yayasan Cahaya Guru said 134 high schools in Jakarta have no Christian religion teacher, and asked for equal rights for followers of indigenous faiths (penghayat kepercayaan). Perisai asked that all teachers, including those at private schools and madrasahs, be paid from the national budget (APBN) and be given access to the P3K selection. A Commission X member described the government's plan: part-time P3K staff become full-time, then gradually become civil servants (PNS) within three years. P2G recalled the Constitutional Court (MK) ruling on separating the education budget from the free nutritious meals program (MBG), and calculated that the education budget excluding MBG in the 2027 state budget (APBN) is only about 14.2 percent.

judul: Plenary Session No. 10: RRI Supervisory Board approved, DPR enters recess
teks: The 10th Plenary Session (Rapat Paripurna) closed Sitting Period I of the 2026-2027 Sitting Year. The session approved Commission VII's report on the fit-and-proper test (uji kelayakan) of 15 candidates for the Supervisory Board of LPP RRI (Radio Republik Indonesia, the public broadcaster) for 2026-2031: five were selected and five were designated as interim replacement candidates (calon pengganti antarwaktu), chosen by the most votes. The session also approved an extension of the deadline for deliberating the Bill on International Civil Law (Hukum Perdata Internasional). In the closing speech, read by a DPR leader on behalf of the DPR Speaker, it was stated that during this sitting period 20 bills were passed into law, 7 bills were approved as DPR initiative proposals, and the 2027 state budget (APBN) was adopted. The DPR enters its recess (reses) from 9 October to 9 November 2026. Plenary session RRI Legislation Recess DPR leaders delivered a letter from the President requesting approval for the sale of state property at the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM), which will be followed up in line with the DPR's rules of procedure. The DPR leaders' consultation meeting has heard a report from BAKN (the DPR's State Accountability Body) on synchronizing the regional budget (APBD) and national budget (APBN) cycles. Commission VII reported on the open fit-and-proper test of 15 candidates for the LPP RRI Supervisory Board and selected five by the most votes. The plenary session approved the five selected candidates and five interim replacement candidates for the LPP RRI Supervisory Board for 2026-2031. The plenary session approved an extension of the deadline for deliberating the Bill on International Civil Law. Closing speech: 20 bills were passed into law, including the Agrarian Reform Regulation Law, the Employment Protection Law and the One Data Law. Closing speech: 13 bills are still in level I deliberation (pembicaraan tingkat I) and will continue in the next sitting period. The DPR enters recess from 9 October to 9 November 2026.

judul: Commission XI has not yet approved the "reasonable" cost standards of LPS, asks for benchmark comparisons first
teks: Commission XI of the DPR (House of Representatives) held a working meeting with Anggito Abimanyu, Chair of the Board of Commissioners of the Deposit Insurance Corporation (Lembaga Penjamin Simpanan, LPS), to discuss a draft LPS Regulation on reasonable standards (standar wajar). Under the LPS Law as amended by Law No. 4 of 2026, LPS's operating budget must follow reasonable standards in the financial services sector, and the regulation requires DPR approval. The standards cover costs, procurement of goods and services, human resources, organization, and remuneration. LPS proposed moving fully from input-based to output-based cost standards by the 2029 budget at the latest, with a special exception for handling failing banks. Commission XI members questioned the definition of "reasonable", the limits of flexibility, what a competitive level of remuneration means, and the absence of any figures in the draft. LPS stated that cost overruns above 5 percent must still go to the DPR. The meeting concluded that approval will only be given after LPS completes a benchmark comparison study, but LPS may prepare its 2027 budget on schedule using its own internal standards. LPS Budget Remuneration Financial sector The meeting agenda was to discuss LPS's reasonable standards under Article 86A of the LPS Law, as most recently amended by Law No. 4 of 2026; the regulation requires DPR approval. LPS Board Chair Anggito Abimanyu set out his principle: being special does not mean being without limits, and being flexible does not mean being without accountability. LPS divides its cost standards into two types: estimates that may be exceeded with strong justification, and ceilings that may not be exceeded. LPS will move from input cost standards (SBM) to performance-based output cost standards (SBK), with a transition period and full implementation targeted for the 2029 annual work plan and budget (RKAT). The standards were drafted using the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, and the Financial Services Authority (OJK) as benchmarks, and will be used for LPS's RKAT starting in 2027. Procurement for liquidation teams, claim-paying banks, and crisis handling is treated as a special case because it must be done quickly. LPS stated that cost overruns are capped at 5 percent; above that, LPS must seek DPR approval. The LPS Deputy Chair said remuneration refers to the 75th percentile of the market. The meeting concluded that further study with a benchmark comparison is needed before approval is given, while LPS may still submit its 2027 RKAT on schedule using its internal reasonable standards.

judul: Commission VIII and the government agree on the 2027 Hajj cost
teks: A working group (Panja) of House Commission VIII of the DPR and the government's own Panja read out and agreed on the conclusions on the Hajj pilgrimage cost (BPIH) for 1448 H/2027 CE. Indonesia's Hajj quota was set at 221,000 people: 92% regular Hajj and 8% special Hajj (haji khusus). The meeting chair said that, after communicating with President Prabowo Subianto, the government will cover Rp3 million of the domestic cost component for each pilgrim. With that subsidy, the average final payment made by pilgrims is reported at around Rp23.2 million, about Rp3 million lower than in 2026. All factions (fraksi) and the government said they agreed. One member asked where the funding for the subsidy would come from. Hajj BPIH Subsidy Hajj quota Indonesia's 2027 Hajj quota was agreed at 221,000 people: regular Hajj 92% (203,320 people) and special Hajj 8% (17,680 people). Exchange rate assumptions used to calculate the cost: 1 US dollar = Rp17,500 and 1 Saudi riyal = Rp4,666.67. The Hajj service contract in Saudi Arabia uses a non-separated scheme, with service package C for pilgrims. The regular Hajj quota is divided among provinces in proportion to each province's waiting list of pilgrims. The meeting chair said the government will cover Rp3 million of the domestic cost component for each pilgrim. The average final payment made by pilgrims, after deducting the initial deposit of Rp25 million and the subsidy, is reported at Rp23,248,825. The factions in Commission VIII and the government said they agreed with the conclusions that were read out.

judul: Legislative Body hears PPMAN: Indigenous Peoples Bill urged to protect Indigenous people and their defenders from criminalization
teks: The DPR's Legislative Body (Baleg) held a public hearing (RDPU) with the Indigenous Peoples' Defenders Association of the Archipelago (Perhimpunan Pembela Masyarakat Adat Nusantara, PPMAN), an advocates' organization that defends Indigenous peoples, on 7 October 2026, one day before the DPR went on its recess (reses). The meeting chair, Martin Manurung, who also chairs the working group (Panja) on the Indigenous Peoples Bill (RUU Masyarakat Adat), said drafting of the bill text will begin after the recess, with the hope of finishing it in Baleg this year. PPMAN asked that the bill include protection from criminalization for Indigenous people and their defenders, an anti-SLAPP principle (protection against lawsuits used to silence critics), and remedies for victims. Members from various factions (fraksi) were supportive, while also discussing how the bill relates to the newly passed Agrarian Reform Regulation Law, the mapping of Indigenous territories, and the role of regional regulations (perda). Indigenous peoples Legislation Criminalization Agrarian reform The hearing (RDPU) made no decisions, so no quorum was required. The attendance list recorded 11 members from 5 factions at the opening. The meeting chair said drafting of the Indigenous Peoples Bill text will begin in the next sitting period after the recess, with the hope of completing it in Baleg this year. PPMAN introduced itself as a wing organization of AMAN (the Indigenous Peoples' Alliance of the Archipelago), with around 203 pro bono advocates and legal experts in 13 provinces. PPMAN said it has assisted around 229 Indigenous peoples' cases over five years, including Indigenous people prosecuted in territorial conflicts and defenders named as suspects. PPMAN stressed that the protection it is asking for is not legal immunity, but a guarantee that criminal law is not used arbitrarily to silence Indigenous peoples. PPMAN proposed an anti-SLAPP principle: legal proceedings must not be used as a tool of retaliation against Indigenous people and their advocates who peacefully fight for their rights. PPMAN proposed seven norms, among them that officials must check the rights status of Indigenous peoples before acting on criminal reports related to territorial conflicts, a mechanism to stop cases that show signs of criminalization, and remedies for victims. Baleg members linked the bill to the newly passed Agrarian Reform Regulation Law, which was said to already contain legal protection for communities and their advocates in resolving agrarian conflicts. Members asked for the mapping of Indigenous territories, because many communities have no written history and no clear boundaries. PPMAN said anti-SLAPP rules already exist in the environmental field, namely Article 66 of Law 32/2009 and Supreme Court Regulation (Perma) 1/2023, along with roughly two hundred regional regulations (perda) recognizing Indigenous peoples. PPMAN stated that the bill actually gives investors certainty through the principle of free, prior and informed consent (FPIC) from Indigenous peoples. Baleg members differed on the recognition mechanism: some felt regional regulations (perda) are still needed, while others proposed a regional head's decree (SK kepala daerah) to make it faster.

judul: Rante Balla land dispute with gold mine in Luwu: House Commission III urges police to act
teks: House Commission III of the DPR (Indonesia's national parliament) held a follow-up hearing (RDP, a hearing with government bodies, and RDPU, a hearing with the public) on a complaint from Anak Adat Rante Balla Menggugat (the Indigenous Descendants of Rante Balla Sue), extended families in Rante Balla Village, Luwu Regency, who claim ancestral land inside the contract-of-work (kontrak karya) gold mining area of PT Masmindo Dwi Area. Attending were the Luwu Regent (Bupati), the Director of General Criminal Investigation (Dirreskrimum) of the South Sulawesi Regional Police (Polda), the Luwu Police Chief (Kapolres), the President Director of PT Masmindo, and family representatives. Luwu Police explained that a report of damage to the fence around the grave of Nepong Titing, lodged in 2021, only moved up to a formal investigation in August 2026. The company said it respects every claim but has no authority to decide who the lawful owner is, and said compensation for the land was paid to the person physically controlling it, based on a land statement letter (SKT). The families said compensation was paid to someone who is not the owner, questioned the term "covered land" (lahan tutupan), and presented five demands. Several Commission III members criticized the police for being slow in handling the reports. The meeting produced five conclusions, including asking the company to temporarily halt activities on the disputed land until an agreement is reached. Agrarian conflict Customary land Gold mining Police The meeting followed up on a public hearing (RDPU) held on 29 September 2026 about the dispute between the Indigenous community or heirs of Rante Balla and PT Masmindo Dwi Area, a gold mining company in Luwu Regency. The complainants said around 45 extended families claim ancestral land within the concession area. The Director of General Criminal Investigation (Dirreskrimum) of the South Sulawesi Police (Polda Sulsel) said the regional police do not directly handle the two police reports related to this case, but provide assistance and supervision for the investigation at Luwu Police. The Luwu Police Chief explained the report on damage to the fence around Nepong Titing's grave, which happened in November 2021: eight witnesses were questioned, the suspect admitted pulling out the fence, and the case moved up to a formal investigation on 26 August 2026. The chair of the meeting asked the police to dig into the motive and who instructed the suspect, rather than stopping at one person. The President Director of PT Masmindo said the company operates under a 1998 contract of work (amended in 2018, expiring in 2050), respects every claim, but has no authority to decide who the lawful owner of the land is. The company said compensation for the claimed land was paid to Eti Poluntu, a former village head, as the person physically controlling the land based on an SKT (land statement letter). A family representative said the names on the land acquisition map had changed from the 1995-1996 owner data, and said the former village head had been convicted by the Makassar Corruption Court (Pengadilan Tipikor) for gratuities connected to land acquisition in the concession area. The families presented five demands, including compensation based on the 1995-1996 owner data, an investigation into the land acquisition process, and a halt to activities on the disputed land. A representative of the Luwu Land Office (BPN) said BPN was not involved in the compensation payment process, and that an SKT is only one piece of evidence that still needs to be verified. Commission III read out five conclusions and said it will hold a follow-up meeting in about one month.

judul: 9th Plenary Session: Manpower Protection Law and One Data Indonesia Law passed
teks: The 9th Plenary Session (Rapat Paripurna) of Sitting Period I of the 2026-2027 Session Year, held on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, opened with 326 of 576 members having signed the attendance list. The Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) submitted its Overview of Audit Results for Semester I (IHPS I) 2026. The session then passed two laws: the Manpower Protection Bill (a DPR initiative, deliberated by Commission IX together with the government) and the One Data Indonesia Bill (deliberated by the Legislation Body, Baleg). The plenary also approved Commission XI's report on the fit-and-proper test of candidates for BPK membership for 2026-2031, and agreed that the factions' views on the Asset Forfeiture Bill would be submitted in writing. Parts of the broadcast, especially the start of the BPK speech and the end of the session, were not clearly captured by the automatic transcript. Plenary Session Manpower One Data BPK Asset forfeiture The attendance list at the opening was signed by 326 of 576 members from all factions, so a quorum was reached. BPK presented IHPS I 2026: the 2025 central government financial statements received an unqualified opinion (WTP, the best audit rating), and 509 of 546 regional governments also received WTP. BPK highlighted three cross-sector issues: upstream oil and gas governance and the institutional status of SKK Migas (the upstream oil and gas regulator), state revenue from foreign worker visas and fisheries, and school operational funds (BOS) and health insurance contributions in the regions. The DPR leadership said the BPK audit results would serve as material for commissions to discuss with their partner institutions. Commission IX's leadership reported on the Manpower Protection Bill: a follow-up to Constitutional Court (MK) Decision No. 168/PUU-XXI/2023, consisting of 23 chapters and 313 articles, with public consultation held on 16-22 September 2026. Commission IX said the balance between workers, employers, and the government in the bill is "masih belum dikatakan ideal" [still cannot be called ideal], but is an important part of protecting workers. The Minister of Manpower, representing the President, detailed the contents of the law: protection for interns, a ban on withholding diplomas, maternity and miscarriage leave with pay, a severance reserve fund, and protection for flexible work. The Legislation Body (Baleg) reported on the One Data Indonesia Bill: 20 chapters and 141 articles, with a One Data administrator that answers to the President and without centralizing data in a single institution. The Minister of National Development Planning/Head of Bappenas, representing the President, expressed agreement and linked the One Data Law to the spirit of the Youth Pledge (Sumpah Pemuda). Commission XI reported on the fit-and-proper test of 23 candidates for BPK membership on 5 October 2026; three candidates did not attend, and two candidates were chosen by deliberation and consensus (musyawarah mufakat). The factions' views on the Asset Forfeiture Bill were agreed to be submitted in writing to the DPR leadership by representatives of eight factions.

judul: Baleg begins deliberating Copyright Bill: 1,117 DIM from the government, target completion 17 December
teks: The House of Representatives' (DPR) Legislation Body (Baleg) held a working meeting on first-level deliberation (pembicaraan tingkat I) of the Copyright Bill with the government on 6 October 2026. Baleg Deputy Chair Martin Manurung explained the bill, which is a DPR initiative. It regulates the economic rights of broadcasters and press companies, works created with artificial intelligence, fair use, and licensing, royalties, and collective management organizations. The bill also follows up on Constitutional Court Decision No. 84/PUU-XXI/2023 so that the definition of a trade center covers the digital realm. The government, represented by the Minister of Law, submitted 1,117 items in its problem inventory list (DIM, Daftar Inventarisasi Masalah). The meeting agreed on a deliberation schedule with a target of finishing no later than 17 December 2026, a deliberation mechanism, and the formation of a working committee (Panja) chaired by Martin Manurung. Legislation Copyright Artificial intelligence Royalties The meeting was attended by 17 members from 8 factions (fraksi); a quorum was declared met and the meeting was open to the public. Martin Manurung explained that the Copyright Bill is a DPR initiative bill that was established at a plenary session on 12 March 2026. The bill follows up on Constitutional Court Decision No. 84/PUU-XXI/2023, which extends the definition of a trade center to the digital realm. The bill's aims: to adapt to the digital era, protect journalistic works, regulate the obligations of digital platforms, and protect traditional cultural expressions and AI-based works. The scope covers the economic rights of broadcasters and the press, AI-based works, fair use, duration of protection, licensing and royalties, disputes, and criminal provisions. The government proposed discussing the institutions of LMK (collective management organizations) and KMKN (the National Collective Management Commission), a royalty endowment fund, the legal status of AI works, and the protection of journalistic works. The government submitted 1,117 DIM: 558 unchanged, 91 amended, 143 proposed for deletion, 181 new substance, and 144 editorial. A member asked the government not to change substance through DIM labeled as repositioning or editorial, citing the deliberation of the One Data Indonesia Bill. The government asked that the Panja meeting not start on 7 October because the Ministry of Law team was hosting a WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization) session in Bali. Baleg leadership stressed that Baleg does not hold closed drafting or deliberation meetings and asked the government to open up public participation.

judul: Satu Data Indonesia Bill approved by all factions in the Legislation Body, heads to plenary session
teks: The DPR's Legislation Body (Baleg) and the government took first-level decisions (keputusan tingkat I) on the Bill on One Data Indonesia (Satu Data Indonesia) on 5 October 2026. Working Committee (Panja) Chair Sturman Panjaitan reported that the agreed bill consists of 20 chapters and 141 articles, after the Panja discussed the government's problem inventory list (DIM) in working committee meetings starting 23 September. The bill sets out the National Core Data (Data Dasar Nasional) as a mandatory reference for planning and budgeting, an One Data administrator answerable to the President, interoperability without physically centralizing data, a classification of data as open, restricted, and closed, security standards set by BSSN (the National Cyber and Crypto Agency), and a role for villages, the TNI (armed forces), the Polri (national police), and corporations as data producers. All factions and the government agreed to take the bill to second-level deliberation (pembicaraan tingkat II) in the plenary session. Legislation One Data Personal data Social assistance The meeting was attended by 28 members from seven factions; a quorum was met and the meeting was open to the public. The Panja Chair reported that the Panja was formed on 23 September 2026 and discussed the bill in seven meetings through 5 October, involving BSSN. The National Core Data was set as the main reference for planning, budgeting, and the distribution of social assistance (bansos), with data classified as open, restricted, and closed. The One Data Indonesia administrator is answerable to the President, replaces the old arrangement, and is coordinative, normative, and facilitative in nature. Interoperability is carried out without physically centralizing databases and without transferring data ownership away from its producers. Access to restricted data may be charged as PNBP (non-tax state revenue), and transfers of closed data outside Indonesia's jurisdiction require the DPR's approval. The agreed bill consists of 20 chapters and 141 articles; the administrator must be established within one year at most. The Gerindra faction welcomed the provision that data sharing between agencies no longer requires a memorandum of understanding. The PKB faction asked that citizens be able to correct their personal data easily and free of charge, and that villages be given full authority to update data. The PKS faction welcomed the requirement to report data security incidents within 1x24 hours at most. Baleg leaders proposed that BSSN and the Geospatial Information Agency (Badan Informasi Geospasial) also attend the plenary session.

judul: 8th Plenary Session: Police Commissioner General Suyudi Ario Seto approved as National Police Chief
teks: The 8th Plenary Session (Rapat Paripurna) of Sitting Period I of the 2026-2027 Session Year was held on Thursday, 1 October 2026, with 383 members attending, according to the attendance list from the Secretariat General. The session approved the report by Commission III on the fit and proper test of the candidate for National Police Chief (Kapolri): General Listyo Sigit Prabowo was honorably discharged, and Police Commissioner General Suyudi Ario Seto was approved as Kapolri. Commission III stated that approval at the commission level was reached by acclamation (aklamasi, agreement without a formal vote) by all factions. The session also designated the Java North Coast Management Authority (Badan Otorita Pengelola Pantai Utara Jawa) as a working partner of Commission IV, and approved an extension of the deadline for deliberating the Industrial Design Bill. Plenary Session National Police Chief North Coast The attendance list recorded 383 members from all factions, so a quorum was reached and the session was opened to the public. The DPR leadership read out the President's letter proposing the dismissal and appointment of the National Police Chief, as well as letters concerning candidates for ambassadors to friendly countries and candidates for the Supervisory Board of LPP RRI (the state public radio broadcaster). The Chair of Commission III reported on the fit and proper test of National Police Chief candidate Police Commissioner General Suyudi Ario Seto, whose vision theme was "polisi bersama masyarakat" [police together with the people] toward Indonesia 2045. Commission III stated that all factions approved by acclamation the appointment of Suyudi Ario Seto and the dismissal of General Listyo Sigit Prabowo. The plenary session approved the honorable discharge of Listyo Sigit Prabowo and the appointment of Suyudi Ario Seto as National Police Chief. The Speaker of the DPR said the decision would be sent to the President promptly, and that the new police chief was planned to be inaugurated after the midday prayer (zuhur) that day. The Java North Coast Management Authority was designated as a working partner of Commission IV of the DPR. The plenary session approved an extension of the deadline for deliberating the Industrial Design Bill at the request of the leadership of the special committee (Pansus).

judul: Commission II and the Ombudsman discuss findings from prison inspections, ask for prison service standards within 30 days
teks: Commission II of the DPR (the House of Representatives) held a hearing (rapat dengar pendapat) with the Ombudsman of the Republic of Indonesia on Tuesday, 29 September 2026, after the Ombudsman's surprise inspection (sidak) of the Class IIA Cibinong Prison drew wide media coverage. The Ombudsman reported inspections at four sites: Pondok Bambu Detention Center, Batam Women's Prison, Tangerang Youth Prison, and Cibinong Prison. Its findings included overcrowding, yellow water, alleged payments to change cells and to use mobile phones, and a lack of facilities for babies. At Cibinong, the team was not allowed in and, according to the Ombudsman, found buildings resembling holiday villas inside the prison grounds. The Chair of Commission II asked the Ombudsman not to handle only one case after another, but to draw up public service standards. The meeting produced five conclusions, including public service standards for prisons within 30 days at the latest. Ombudsman Prisons Corrections Public services The Chair of Commission II said the Ombudsman's budget for next year will roughly double, from about Rp213 billion to Rp415 billion. The Chair of Commission II asked the Ombudsman to return to its core task: not to be busy with one case after another, but to give permanent recommendations for improving public services. Commission II summoned the Ombudsman directly, rather than going through Commission XIII, so that it would not look like it was setting the Ombudsman against the Ministry of Immigration and Corrections. The Ombudsman said the inspections were prompted by information on social media about alleged cell rentals and illegal payments, as well as a rise in public complaints about the corrections system (pemasyarakatan). At Pondok Bambu Detention Center, the Ombudsman found an overcrowded block, yellow water, expired fire extinguishers, and information from inmates about a payment of Rp500,000 to move cells and Rp250,000 to use a mobile phone. At Batam Women's Prison, the Ombudsman found expensive prices at the prison cooperative, unfit mattresses, toilets without partitions, flooding when it rains, and inmates' babies who had not received milk, diapers, and immunizations. At Tangerang Youth Prison, the Ombudsman found overcrowding, water smelling of rust, small food portions, and a clinic open only from morning to midday. At Cibinong Prison, the Ombudsman team was refused entry twice. From outside the grounds, the team noted a section without a fence, two luxury cars, liquor bottles, buildings that the Ombudsman said resembled villas, and information about a payment of Rp150,000 per week. The Ombudsman called the Cibinong case the tip of the iceberg and asked the Ministry of Immigration and Corrections for a thorough evaluation from top to bottom, including staff welfare. The Ombudsman said the Minister of Immigration and Corrections had contacted them and was ready to collaborate. Its suggestions for improvement have not yet been handed over because the meeting with the Minister was postponed. A member reminded the meeting that Article 44 of the Ombudsman Law sets criminal penalties for anyone who obstructs the Ombudsman's oversight. A member who used to be a corrections officer asked that the findings not be generalized, and said the root of the problem is systemic: the food allowance for inmates is Rp20,000 compared with Rp40,000 for police detainees, and there is no risk allowance for officers. Commission II agreed to set up an "Ombudsman corner" at each member's constituency aspiration house (rumah aspirasi) starting next year to receive public complaints.

judul: Budget Committee and government agree on 2027 state budget: 2.4 percent deficit, Rp4,106 trillion in spending
teks: The DPR Budget Committee (Badan Anggaran, or Banggar) and the government (the Finance Minister, the Minister of National Development Planning/Head of Bappenas, the Ministry of Law, and Bank Indonesia) completed first-level deliberations (pembicaraan tingkat I) on the 2027 State Budget Bill (RUU APBN) on 24 September 2026. Four working groups (panitia kerja, or Panja) reported agreement on: basic macroeconomic assumptions with 6 percent growth, state revenue of around Rp3,435 trillion, state spending of around Rp4,106 trillion, a deficit of 2.4 percent of GDP, transfers to regions of Rp735 trillion, and an education budget of 20.07 percent of state spending. The draft bill also adds provisions requiring DPR approval for a number of budget and financing changes. The party factions' mini opinions (pendapat mini fraksi) were submitted in writing, the government stated its agreement, and the bill was sent on to the plenary session (rapat paripurna). 2027 State Budget Budget Subsidies Transfers to regions Education budget The 2027 basic assumptions agreed: economic growth of 6 percent, inflation of 2.5 percent, an exchange rate of Rp17,500 per US dollar, a government bond (SBN) yield of 6.9 percent, and an oil price (ICP, the Indonesian Crude Price) of 75 US dollars per barrel. Development targets for 2027 include a poverty rate of 6 to 6.5 percent, extreme poverty of 0 to 0.5 percent, open unemployment of 4.3 to 4.87 percent, and 2.57 to 3.49 million new jobs. State revenue was agreed at around Rp3,435 trillion, about Rp9 trillion higher than the draft budget (RAPBN) proposal; the tax target is around Rp2,912 trillion and non-tax state revenue (PNBP) around Rp522 trillion. Energy subsidies were agreed at around Rp261.5 trillion, about Rp11.4 trillion lower than the draft budget proposal. The 2027 budget deficit was agreed at around Rp671.2 trillion, or 2.4 percent of GDP. Central government spending was agreed at around Rp3,371 trillion; spending by ministries and agencies rose by around Rp52 trillion from the government's proposal, while non-ministry spending fell. The education budget was agreed at around Rp824 trillion, or 20.07 percent of total state spending. Transfers to regions were agreed at Rp735 trillion, including the General Allocation Fund (DAU) of Rp415 trillion and the Special Allocation Fund (DAK) of around Rp159.4 trillion. Part of the DAU and village funds are directed to support the Red and White Village and Urban Ward Cooperatives (Koperasi Kelurahan dan Desa Merah Putih). A scheme was agreed under which the central government finances regional infrastructure development, taking into account unpaid revenue-sharing funds (dana bagi hasil), so that it does not add to the burden on regional budgets (APBD). The draft bill adds that creative financing that burdens the state budget, the use of the excess budget balance (SAL), and changes to spending details through Presidential Regulations (Peraturan Presiden) must receive DPR approval. The Rp39 trillion education financing item was broken down as: the Education Endowment Fund (Dana Abadi Pendidikan) Rp25 trillion, the Garuda Elite Schools Endowment Fund (Dana Abadi Sekolah Unggul Garuda) Rp8 trillion, and other education endowment funds Rp6 trillion. The Finance Minister, speaking for the government, said the 2027 fiscal policy is designed to be expansionary yet still disciplined, and that the 2.4 percent deficit will be maintained.
